adoption_candidates: ASC-38: agy output table emits only empty, deny, continue or injectSteps (never allow or '{}'), independently matching G1's measured agy facts.
ASC-03: acceptance oracle kept outside the agent-writable tree and digest-pinned before, during and after verification.
ASC-04: graders must observe expected outputs; an exit(0) stub or emptied test must fail, so exit 0 alone never proves a criterion.
ASC-15: a sticky gap counter (stepIdx contiguity, Pre/Post pairing, transcript parse) makes completion fail closed when G1's fact log is incomplete.
ASC-16: tri-state facts and tool calls; unknown never satisfies a completion predicate.
ASC-11: deterministic protected-path deny in PreToolUse for both hooks.json files, G1 state, contract and pinned oracles.
ASC-17: static evidence-basis table so only G1-produced deterministic facts may deny or continue.
ASC-22: pass requires exit 0, no timeout, untruncated output and an unchanged tree across the run.
ASC-02: discard results if contract, intent or tree identity changed mid-run, and count skipped or side-effect checks as failed.
ASC-45: captured host payloads and transcripts as SHA-256-pinned fixtures; a recapture diff is the host-contract re-test.
ASC-05: receipts pin G1 evaluator version and the merged hook-policy hash; later events void them.
ASC-55: independent conformance verifier plus a mutation suite that must reject forged, stale or tool-origin evidence.
ASC-27: strict-shrink progress over comparable G1-run checks as the Stop controller's displacement signal.
ASC-31: persisted, never-decreasing count of G1's own continuations, stopping after k zero-displacement turns well below agy's 10.
ASC-06: imported or remembered evidence is history until G1 recomputes its key against the current tree and contract.
ASC-51: Wilson intervals, paired cluster bootstrap and withholding rules for host-contract re-tests and injection A/B tests.
ASC-50: deterministic hash-assigned experiment arms with a silent control arm (fix the 6/5/5 modulo bias).
ASC-19: every regex the adapter uses ships with must-match and must-not-match vectors checked at load.
ASC-44: per-event payload-shape schema for agy 1.1.27, calibrated on captured payloads of every tool type, failing closed for completion.
ASC-30: revisit detection on whole-tree hashes as the oscillation input that ends Stop continuations.
ASC-07: strict contract decoding plus a criteria-by-checks coverage matrix that rejects manual-only criteria.
ASC-21: receipt key with contract hash, scrubbed-env digest and runner version where an empty field means unknown.
ASC-12: replace test-weakening regexes with SHA-256 pinning of oracle files (tests, conftest, test configs).
ASC-13: deny publish/release/tag-push unless the latest G1 receipt passed on the current tree hash.
ASC-26: control state as a pure, idempotent fold over the ledger, with an incremental-equals-rescan property test.
risks: Completion enforcement is off by default: in 'recommend' mode s5.stop_unmet can never block because its advice is only produced inside the block branch, so a false 'done' ends the turn; blocking needs validated mode with an operator digest (internal/live/hooks.go:700, internal/policy/rollout.go:22, internal/live/session.go:695, internal/live/live_test.go:279).

Stop gate fails open on skipped or side-effect checks, a draft or stale contract (an agent write to contract.yml resets acceptance to draft), queue gaps, and checks exceeding the 150 s client wait (internal/live/hooks.go:707, internal/live/hooks.go:670, internal/live/session.go:783, internal/live/session.go:769, internal/hookclient/hookclient.go:31).

Every hook failure is fail-open: the client prints nothing on any error or after the 15 ms PreToolUse budget, so a slow or dead daemon silently disables all gates; under agy, where PreToolUse timeouts block, the semantics differ from samcheonpo's assumptions (internal/hookclient/hookclient.go:1, internal/hookclient/hookclient.go:141, README.en.md:290).

Likely agy bug (static inference, untested): non-shell agy PostToolUse events carry no tool_response, hookShape treats that as payload drift, and markShapeBad drops every agy session to observe-only until the daemon restarts (internal/live/agy.go:78, internal/live/hookshape.go:60, internal/live/hookshape.go:81).

agy version mismatch: fixtures and capability profile cover agy 1.3.x, not G1's 1.1.27; the installer registers no SessionStart or PostInvocation, uses matcher '*' (an invalid regex if matchers are regexes), and bakes in an absolute binary path whose absence would make agy's fail-closed PreToolUse block every call (internal/adapter/caps.go:73, internal/install/jsonhooks.go:179, internal/install/jsonhooks.go:41, internal/live/agy.go:13).

Same-OS-user trust boundary: any agent-run process can talk to the daemon socket (Command accept/keep/extend, forged hook events, Shutdown that resets in-memory escalation state), read acceptance.key to forge contract acceptance, and recompute ledger hashes (internal/live/daemon.go:342, internal/live/daemon.go:369, internal/contract/contract.go:393, internal/live/session.go:101, README.en.md:292, docs/spec/progress-contract-v2-draft.md:57).

The agent-writable project file .samcheonpo.yml can lower the rollout mode to shadow and the block cap to 0 for the next session, and it is not in the watched config list; unknown YAML keys are silently ignored (internal/config/config.go:329, internal/config/config.go:333, internal/config/config.go:282).
An observation gap suppresses all hook output, including protected-path, budget and ceiling denies (internal/live/hooks.go:80).

Ledger is mutable and unanchored: session rows are deleted and re-inserted per analysis, seals are INSERT OR REPLACE, the head lives in the same database, and non-accepted contract states (skipped, done) are not MAC-checked (internal/ledger/ledger.go:160, internal/ledger/ledger.go:217, internal/contract/contract.go:379).

Network egress when enabled: optional LLM judge via the Anthropic SDK (default model claude-haiku-4-5) or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and push notifications to public ntfy.sh by default once a topic is set; desktop notifications are on by default and spawn notify-send/osascript/PowerShell (internal/judge/judge.go:127, internal/judge/judge.go:206, internal/notify/notify.go:64, internal/notify/notify.go:43, internal/config/config.go:241, go.mod:6).

Prompt-injection surfaces: the judge prompt embeds agent-authored command summaries and parses labels by substring; the anchor parser accepts the tag anywhere and SKILL.md tells the agent to adopt any ANCHOR line; repository CI 'run:' lines are injected into the contract draft request (internal/live/session.go:1213, internal/judge/judge.go:159, internal/hookclient/anchor.go:74, plugins/claude-code/skills/samcheonpo/SKILL.md:88, internal/contract/contract.go:620).

Imperative agent-facing text: the draft note tells the agent not to wait for acceptance, the capability-limit prescription suggests switching to a stronger model, and SKILL.md instructs downloading and installing release binaries (internal/live/hooks.go:321, internal/intervene/templates/ko/s6.capability_limit.rx.tmpl:1, plugins/claude-code/skills/samcheonpo/SKILL.md:16).

Remedy command injection: subjects extracted from untrusted tool output (module names, URLs) are substituted unsanitized into commands presented for a human to run (internal/fp/failclass.go:71, internal/fp/failclass.go:238, internal/intervene/templates/ko/s2.environment.user.tmpl:3).

External programs run outside agent permission prompts: iron-laws resolved from PATH after every write (enabled by default), '<agent> --version' probes, git inside the agent-controlled repository (repo-local git config such as fsmonitor or filters applies), and desktop notifiers (internal/live/ironlaws.go:39, internal/config/config.go:245, internal/adapter/caps.go:176, internal/live/ws.go:165).
Checks run with the daemon's unscrubbed environment, and non-worktree checks run in the live project directory (internal/live/verification_plan.go:80, internal/live/checkpoint.go:126).

Transcript-derived evidence is spoofable: the agy transcript is a file the agent's shell can write, an unresolved agy result is recorded as success at a final flush, and legacy Codex exit codes take the first regex match in program output (internal/live/agy.go:173, internal/live/agy.go:122, internal/adapter/codex/parser.go:516).

Weak identifiers: fingerprints and authority keys are SHA-256 truncated to 128 bits, receipts show a 12-hex seal prefix, and rollback plan ids are 32-bit (internal/fp/fp.go:18, internal/seal/seal.go:46, internal/live/rollback.go:367).

Privacy: the ledger stores plaintext paths, an 80-character first prompt, full goals, check commands and verdict messages; the store_raw_text option is declared but unused (internal/ledger/ledger.go:170, internal/ledger/ledger.go:187, internal/config/config.go:184).

Classifier false negatives (env rm, command rm, docker exec, find -delete, git clean, bash -c, python -c) leave the workspace fingerprint unchanged, and agent-writable verify_commands skip write detection (internal/classify/classify.go:71, internal/classify/classify.go:170).

Bench graders and replay tasks execute candidate or agent-typed code with the full user environment and are not sandboxed; the Windows VM script downloads unpinned toolchains and CI uses mutable action tags (internal/bench/live.go:311, docs/benchmarks/protocol-v1.md:17, scripts/windows-vm-test.sh:91, .github/workflows/ci.yml:16).

Quality: experiment arms use hex[0] % 3 (a 6/5/5 split), the conformance level check compares strings lexicographically, semantic oscillation conflates identifier/literal-only fixes, the claim regex misses 'Fixed the failing test. Done.', and code comments contradict code on version gating and probe timeouts (internal/detect/engine.go:1600, cmd/samcheonpo-conformance/main.go:137, internal/detect/ast_oscillation.go:163, internal/detect/bypass.go:143, internal/adapter/caps.go:33, docs/spec/hook-startup.md:33).
Language and pricing fit: all injected templates are Korean-only, and there are no Gemini price rows, so agy usage is always unpriced (internal/intervene/intervene.go:19, internal/cost/prices.yml:7).

Evidence is mostly unit, fixture and synthetic-scenario tests: real-agent verification is claimed only for repeated-failure nudges and blocks (including agy) and a few Claude Code features, while waiting/stall advice and most long-session rules are unverified with real agents (docs/support-matrix.md:55, docs/support-matrix.md:58, docs/support-matrix.md:61).
Effectiveness is unproven by the authors' own account: small samples, no general savings claim, effectiveness_validated=false (README.en.md:288, internal/eval/corpus.go:375).
